transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-20
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Maria Gomez (CISO - Mapleton), Alan Walker (Head of ML), Sasha Li (Compliance), Derek Chan (Platform)

---
Summary (auto): Redwood reviews compliance posture and explicit data handling guarantees. Customer requests docs and contractual language to ensure no training and proper PHI treatment.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'll kick off, uh, this is Jordan from Redwood Inference, with Priya on the call. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Maria: Hi Jordan, good thanks. We wanted to cover SOC 2, data residency, and make sure the "no training" bit is explicit.
[00:12] Priya: Yes -- we'll go through our posture and then demo where logs live and how you can control retention. Quick note, transcript might have a few noise words because of the recorder.
[00:22] Alan: Sounds good. On the ML side we care about any implicit retention, KV cache, and whether prompts could possibly be used to fine-tune models.
[00:30] Jordan: Absolutely. Top-line: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II in prod, we also maintain ISO 27001 cert for our control plane -- Priya do you want to add details on scope?
[00:38] Priya: Sure. SOC 2 Type II covers our hosted API and the control plane; Dedicated and Private deployments have different scoping — for Private (VPC/on-prem) customers you can elect to run the inference runtime in your VPC which isolates data from our hosted multitenant environment. The ISO cert mostly covers the control plane operations.
[00:55] Sasha: Quick question — does SOC 2 Type II include our logs? We need to show auditability for access to PHI.
[00:59] Priya: The SOC report covers controls around access, logging and change management. For proof, we can provide snippets and the actual report. The audit logs we capture include API calls (request metadata), admin console actions, and key rotation events. We retain audit logs by default for 365 days; can be exported into your SIEM.
[01:25] Derek: When you say "request metadata" do you also store full prompts or do you strip them?
[01:30] Priya: We capture request headers and metadata for routing and billing. Prompt storage depends on configuration — default hosted retention is 30 days for debugging and quality. But for Dedicated/Private, you can set retention to zero or disable retention entirely. Also we offer an option to redact or hash PII before material gets stored.
[01:52] Maria: So default 30 days — is that overwritten by our contract for the pilot? We want no prompt retention at all.
[01:58] Jordan: Yes, that can be contracted. For the pilot we can disable retention or configure retention to 0 and ensure logs are forwarded to your SIEM. We'll include that in the pilot SOW.
[02:10] Alan: I want explicit confirmation: do you use any customer-submitted prompts to fine-tune or train models downstream?
[02:15] Priya: Short answer: no. Redwood does not use customer prompts or content to train shared models. We have an explicit policy that customer data is not used for model training unless a customer opts in via an enterprise program. We can provide the policy text for contracts.
[02:30] Maria: Can you provide the wording we can include in our procurement docs?
[02:33] Jordan: We'll send a suggested clause. We should be clear: hosted customers — we segregate data and default non-training applies; if customer chooses to opt-in to training there's an explicit opt-in flow and legal sign-off.
[02:46] Sasha: About encryption: is all data encrypted at rest and in transit? And can we bring our own keys?
[02:52] Priya: Yes, TLS in transit and AES-256 at rest. For Dedicated & Private, we support customer-managed KMS keys (CMEK) via AWS KMS and GCP KMS; HSM-backed keys are available for on-prem. Key rotation events are logged in audit trails. Note: sometimes the recorder transcribed KMS as K S M, but it's KMS.
[03:15] Derek: For VPC/private deployment, does Redwood ship a package or do you deploy the runtime as an image? We have air-gapped infra in some regions.
[03:22] Priya: For private/on-prem we provide a containerized runtime and deployment guide; for fully air-gapped customers we do an offline install with a separate support package. We'll share the network diagram and install checklist.
[03:37] Alan: On PII/PHI, does Redwood offer automated de-id plugins or do we need to pre-process?
[03:43] Priya: We have a few options: pre-processing at customer side is recommended for the highest control; on the platform we can configure redaction rules and a PII scrubber which will mask specific entities before storing. For PHI specifically, customers usually use Private deployment and send minimal identifiers; we also support Data Loss Prevention (DLP) hooks to block certain categories.
[04:05] Maria: We will need to show our auditors that access to PHI is restricted and logged. How do you do RBAC and SSO?
[04:11] Jordan: Redwood supports SSO via SAML and OIDC; RBAC is role-based with custom roles and least-privilege policies. Admin actions, key management, model rollouts — all are gated behind roles. We'll provide a sample RBAC matrix.
[04:25] Sasha: Can we get a demo of the audit log UI and export?
[04:29] Priya: Yes — in the tech deep-dive I'll walk through the console where you can filter by user, by resource, by API key and export logs as JSON/CSV. We also support streaming audit logs to your SIEM via syslog/HTTP.
[04:45] Alan: Regarding data residency: can you enforce region lock so tokens never leave eu-west-1 for EU customers?
[04:52] Priya: For hosted we have region controls; for strict residency we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments which run entirely in the selected region or your VPC. We'll note any cross-zone control plane metadata that could be relevant.
[05:07] Maria: Ok, practical question: if a user submits a PHI-containing prompt to your hosted API, what logs will we see and what will Redwood store by default?
[05:16] Priya: We'll see request metadata (time, region, model used, request ID); full prompt content is stored only if retention is enabled. For PHI, best practice is to disable storage and stream logs to your SIEM and/or preprocess client-side to redact PHI. We can also set up a retention policy of 0 days for the pilot.
[05:36] Derek: How about backups and snapshots? If you keep backups, could they contain prompts?
[05:41] Priya: Backups can contain encrypted data; for Private deployments, backups live in your environment and are under your KMS. For hosted, backups are encrypted with service-managed keys unless you provide CMEK. We can add backup retention and scope to the contract.
[05:58] Maria: We want contractual guarantees. Can you provide a template with explicit "no training on customer data" sentence and the option to opt into training with separate paperwork?
[06:07] Jordan: Yes — we'll send suggested legal language and mark the opt-in process. We'll also include operational details showing how retention is disabled and how logs are exported for audits.
[06:17] Sasha: A note from compliance — we also need an explanation on how token-level logs are handled: are responses stored? Is the full completion logged or only generated token counts?
[06:26] Priya: By default we store the full completion for debugging for 30 days (hosted). You can configure to only store aggregates (token counts) and metadata; response bodies can be redacted or omitted. All those settings are available per-tenant for Dedicated/Private.
[06:43] Alan: Are prompts ever used to improve model serving performance (like cache warm-ups) that could persist data?
[06:49] Priya: We do automatic KV cache management for runtime performance, but that cache is ephemeral and tied to the runtime instance; it is not persisted to training datasets. For Dedicated/Private you control cache lifetimes and whether caching is enabled.
[07:03] Maria: About incident response — if there's a suspected data exfiltration event, what's your SR?
[07:09] Jordan: We have an incident response plan aligned with our SOC controls. We notify affected customers per contract, provide root cause analysis, and we've got playbooks for containment. We'll share the incident playbook redacted for public consumption.
[07:24] Sasha: Does Redwood undergo annual penetration testing and vulnerability scanning?
[07:28] Priya: Yes; we have internal vuln scanning and annual third-party pentests. The pen test summary can be shared under an NDA — I'll put that in the artifacts.
[07:40] Derek: About API keys — can we enforce hardware-backed keys or rotate keys frequently?
[07:46] Priya: API keys can be rotated; for extra security we support short-lived credentials and can integrate with your identity provider. For HSM-backed keys, that's part of the private/HSM offering.
[07:57] Alan: Do you have a single-tenant offering versus multi-tenant for the runtime?
[08:01] Priya: Dedicated gives you reserved capacity on isolated GPU pools; Private gives you your own runtime in your VPC or on-prem which is effectively single-tenant. We'll send the capacity and SLA sheet.
[08:14] Maria: OK let's talk about evidence. We need SOC 2 artifacts, pen test summary, KMS architecture diagram, and suggested contract text.
[08:21] Jordan: We'll upload the SOC 2 Type II report, the pen test summary under NDA, a KMS diagram, and suggested contractual language.
[08:28] Sasha: Also please include a sample RBAC matrix and the admin role audit logs sample.
[08:32] Priya: Will do. For the RBAC matrix, roles include: reader, developer, admin, key-admin, billing. Each role has specific permissions; we can map to your internal roles.
[08:46] Alan: One more technical: how do you isolate model artifacts? If we pin a model version, could models be shared across tenants?
[08:53] Priya: Model artifacts are versioned and can be pinned. In hosted we may use shared model files on disk but access is logically restricted; in Dedicated/Private you can bring and pin model binaries into your environment, guaranteeing no cross-tenant mixing.
[09:06] Maria: Great. Anything we missed?
[09:09] Jordan: I want to reiterate the 3 key points: 1) Redwood will not use customer content for model training unless customer opts in; 2) retention and logging policies are configurable and can be set to zero; 3) Dedicated/Private options exist for strict residency and single-tenant needs.
[09:27] Maria: That covers the main items. We'll expect the docs and draft clause.
[09:31] Jordan: Perfect. Next we'll schedule the tech deep-dive; Priya will run the logs and KMS rotation demo.
[09:37] Priya: I'll send a calendar invite for the deep-dive and include instructions for a short pre-demo checklist (accounts, sample tokens that are safe to use).
[09:46] Alan: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[09:48] Jordan: Thanks — we'll follow up with the artifacts.
[09:52] (call ends)
